findings.title: The ledger doesn't pin the per-key order of acquire, decide, and release, or what releases a key when a decision raises
findings.why_it_matters: Summary reads as acquire-all-then-decide while D1 implies per-key; neither says what releases a key when a decision raises or is cancelled, so R can behave like H and AppKeyLock claims can drift.
findings.chosen: Rewrite the Summary's Lock move bullet as strictly per-key acquire/decide/release-or-keep, released exactly once including on raise or cancel

findings.title: Deciding no-op keys under the lock makes the batch wait behind in-flight HTTP actions on keys it ends up not touching
findings.why_it_matters: A batch can now park on a no-op key under an HTTP action, holding earlier restart keys and _change_event_lock, bounded by stop deadlines.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a batch can wait, up to the stop deadlines, behind an in-flight HTTP action on a key whose plan comes out empty, holding its earlier restart keys and `_change_event_lock` meanwhile
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a batch can wait, up to the stop deadlines, behind an in-flight HTTP action on a key whose plan comes out empty, holding its earlier restart keys and `_change_event_lock` meanwhile

findings.title: The gate keys on `(app_key, index)`, but a flagged instance's leftover work is keyed on its instance name
findings.why_it_matters: A rename onto a flagged instance's name creates a live instance sharing owner registries with a zombie until restart.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a config edit that moves a flagged instance's name to another index or app creates a live instance that shares owner registries with the zombie until hassette restarts
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a config edit that moves a flagged instance's name to another index or app creates a live instance that shares owner registries with the zombie until hassette restarts

findings.title: An app with one flagged index and its other indices stopped still gets a forced module re-import
findings.why_it_matters: force_reload guard counts only running instances, so a partly flagged app re-imports its module while the zombie runs old code.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a partially flagged app's module is still re-imported for its healthy siblings while the zombie runs the old class until restart
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a partially flagged app's module is still re-imported for its healthy siblings while the zombie runs the old class until restart

findings.title: The ledger doesn't say what the refusal ERROR contains, and two funnels will write it independently
findings.why_it_matters: Two hand-written refusal messages drift, and a thin line repeated on every save doesn't link back to the flag reason.
findings.recommended: A: One shared formatter over the `NeedsRestartRecord` (instance name, app key, index, original reason, `flagged_at`), called by both funnels
findings.chosen: A: One shared formatter over the `NeedsRestartRecord` (instance name, app key, index, original reason, `flagged_at`), called by both funnels
findings.choice_reason: Auto-picked as clear-cut per standing preference; surfaced to user

findings.title: A flagged-only app with autostart=false skips config edits at DEBUG instead of reaching the gate
findings.why_it_matters: A config edit to a flagged-only autostart=false app is neither applied nor refused loudly.
findings.chosen: Side A: keep the skip, document it
findings.choice_reason: when autostart is false i don't want anything starting it except me pressing the button or running a command

findings.title: "No flag means safe to replace" ignores stops that fail before a teardown report exists
